chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, that he asked him about the man who is injected, being ill, in the month of Ramadan.
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The fasting one, it is not allowed for him to be injected.'

key_terms.لَا يَجُوزُ: it is not allowed / not permissible

ai.seo_question: Does an injection break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the ruling on *ihtiqan* (rectal administration of medicine) during Ramadan, with the Imam declaring it impermissible (*lā yajuzu*) for the fasting person. While some jurists debate whether this breaks the fast due to the opening of the *fajj* (passageway) or merely constitutes a disliked act, the text emphasizes the prohibition of introducing substances via the rectum during daylight hours. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between rectal and nasal/ear administration, where the latter is often considered valid if the substance does not reach the brain.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who asked about the man who is injected as he happens to be with the illness during the Month of Ramazan.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fasting one, it is not allowed for him that he injects’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs an enema because of an illness in the month of Ramadan.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Performing an enema is not permissible when fasting.’”
